I spent over two months hiking and mountain climbing in -40C temperatures in Tibet.

I walked out of Tibet across the Nepalese border and crashed in the first hostel I came across. I didn't actually crash because I'd become accustomed to very high altitudes and was literally able to run almost indefinitely at lower altitudes without panting... I was Superman!

Anyhoo... I'd been eating cubes of butter, icing sugar, protein bars, bread, vitamins, oats and instant noodles (when I had the energy to light a gas fire) for two months. Have you ever tried eating a slice of bread out of the freezer? Well, your freezer is a warm fireplace compared to the -40 degrees centigrade conditions even at Everest base-camp. It's worse than eating an ice-cube... in conditions where the inside of your mouth starts to freeze if you keep it open and your piss freezes before it hits the ground and where you'd lose all of your fingernails if your glove came off for more than a few minutes. It's so cold your skin feels like it's burning... because it is.

The next morning, I went to the hostel's community dining area and there it was: community Kellogg's Corn Flakes and pasteurized cow's milk! I wept.

It was the happiest moment of my life.

When writing, I'm frequently annoyed by idiosyncrasies of English where there doesn't seem to be an appropriate singular pronoun that's indefinite regarding gender.

E.g. if I wrote "Atko held the apple up to the light, the way a shopper might inspect [his/her/its/their] grocer's produce.":

His doesn't make sense because not all shoppers are male.

Her doesn't make sense because not all shoppers are male.

Its doesn't make sense because shoppers aren't genderless.

Their sounds kludgy because it's really a plural being used for a singular shopper.

Any suggestions fellow goats? Is there a different way I can structure sentences to avoid the awkward their-as-a-singular phrasing? Is there a pronoun I havent thought of that I could use instead? (And if you suggest "zhe" or somesuch I'll slap you back to whatever safe space you came from).
Suggestions for possessive pronouns when I dont want to specify gender, without sounding like I should have blue hair and a hyphenated studies degree?
Atko held the apple up to the light, the way a shopper might inspect his or her grocer's produce
In my opinion his, her or their would all work. If I read any of the three I wouldn't give it a second thought.

Sometimes you can use they and their or you can use he or she/his or her.

you could drop the possessive part and just say "...the way a shopper might inspect the grocer's produce."

This is probably your best bet. English doesn't have gender neutral pronouns that are appropriate to address a person but all nouns are inherently neutral.
